news.author: Garrett Ball
news.title: Harrison Smith returning to Vikings on one-year deal
news.desc: Harrison Smith is returning to the Vikings on a one-year, $12.5 million deal.
news.impact: Smith is a Minnesota stalwart and franchise legend. He will provide Brian Flores' secondary with a veteran presence and ability.

news.author: Garrett Ball
news.title: Jon Weeks promoted to Niners active roster
news.desc: Jon Weeks has been promoted to the Niners active roster. In a corresponding move, Brayden Willis has been released.
news.impact: Weeks will provide some special teams depth and the exit of Willis implies the return of George Kittle.

news.author: Garrett Ball
news.title: Brayden Willis waived by Niners
news.desc: Brayden Willis has been waived by the 49ers. In a corresponding move, they promoted long snapper Jon Weeks to the active roster.
news.impact: Willis' waiving likely signals the return of George Kittle, with Weeks providing some special teams depth. Willis is likely to be irrelevant for fantasy this season.

news.author: Garrett Ball
news.title: TreVeyon Henderson (ankle) not practicing Saturday
news.desc: TreVeyon Henderson (ankle) was not practicing Saturday.
news.impact: Henderson has not practiced since August 24th, not a great sign for his availability come game time. The Patriots play the Seahawks on Wednesday, rather than a Thursday, giving Henderson one less day to get healthy. The Patriots first injury report comes out later today.

news.author: Jordan Epp
news.title: Josh Jacobs has court appearance date moved up
news.desc: Green Bay Packers running back Josh Jacobs had his initial court appearance moved up to Sept. 10 from Nov. 17 regarding Jacobs' misdemeanor charges.
news.impact: Jacobs was charged with battery and criminal destruction of property and is scheduled to appear at the Brown County courthouse on Sept. 10, multiple days before Green Bay's season opener against Minnesota. It is unclear how this will affect his return timeline; Jacobs is currently on the commissioner's exempt list, with a potential suspension looming.

news.author: Jordan Epp
news.title: J.K. Dobbins will maintain Denver's RB1 role in 2026
news.desc: Running back J.K. Dobbins will "for sure" be the Denver Broncos' lead back this season, with three players set to have roles in the backfield, according to Zac Stevens of DNVR Sports.
news.impact: Dobbins was very successful in 2025 when he was healthy, averaging 5.0 yards per carry and rushing for 772 yards in 10 games. RJ Harvey and rookie Jonah Coleman will have roles, a regular trait for head coach Sean Payton's offenses. Due to injury risk and a congested backfield, Dobbins has a deflated ADP price as the half-PPR RB34, according to FantasyPros.

news.author: Jordan Epp
news.title: Parker Washington, Jaguars remain in contract talks
news.desc: The Jacksonville Jaguars are "not going to stop talking" to wide receiver Parker Washington as both sides iron out a potential contract extension, says general manager James Gladstone.
news.impact: Gladstone said the team would not hesitate to carry contract discussions into the regular season as they aim to finalize a deal with their breakout wideout. Washington had 58 receptions for 847 yards and five touchdowns last season and carries an expert consensus ranking of WR29, according to FantasPros, into his fourth NFL season.

news.author: Jordan Epp
news.title: Christian Gonzalez, Patriots 'remain apart' on contract
news.desc: New England Patriots cornerback Christian Gonzalez and the team "remain apart on several key elements" amid extension discussions ahead of the season opener.
news.impact: Gonzalez was noncommittal on his status for Week 1 amid contract disputes, which could put pressure on the Patriots to finish the deal. Some groundwork has been laid, and Gonzalez is expected to become the league's highest-paid cornerback, but finer details of the contract structure need to be finalized.

news.author: Jordan Epp
news.title: Tua Tagovailoa: Falcons could name starting QB soon
news.desc: The Atlanta Falcons could name their starting quarterback, between Tua Tagovailoa and Michael Penix Jr., as early as Monday, Sept. 7, ahead of Week 1.
news.impact: Nearly every team has named its starter for Week 1, but Atlanta has not formally announced its QB1. According to Ian Rapoport, Tagovailoa could have a "short leash" if named the starter as Atlanta waits for Penix to get healthy. Ideally, the Falcons hoped Tagovailoa would prove himself to be a steady, veteran presence, but Atlanta finds itself in limbo under center.

news.author: Ari Koslow
news.title: Aaron Donald uncertain for Week 1
news.desc: Rams DL Aaron Donald is uncertain for the season opener next Thursday against the 49ers.
news.impact: Rams coach Sean McVay said he expects every player to travel with the team to Australia, which includes Donald. If he is cleared to play, it is likely he'll be on some sort of snap count.
